newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE cocoa bounces up again in thin volume.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE cocoa bounces up again in thin volume.

text.p: LIFFE cocoa futures flipped higher in an afternoon wave of short-covering on Tuesday, further securing their position above a critical chart gap, but volume was thin.
"We looked for a downside correction and we didn't get it. Then they were all short and they had to cover," said one trader.
"But there was no volume on the way up," he added.

After spending the morning session in negative territory, benchmark May cocoa bounced higher in sympathy with a recovery in New York. It saw an intraday high of 1,019 stg per tonne after a morning dip to 997, but ended off the session peak at 1,016 stg, up 11 stg on the day.
Most forward contracts recorded smaller gains, although turnover totalled a slim 3,310 lots including 400 lots of against actuals and some 1,000 crosses, traders said.
Truxo and Rudolf Wolff led the buyers in the afternoon. Mees Pierson was said to be selling December while Cargill bought September.
Producers and industry were sidelined while the market continued to browse around the 1,000 stg level looking for direction after last week's spike to 1,048 stg.
Traders said the afternoon rebound was probably spearheaded by New York where the May contract stood $19 higher at $1,447 at 1730 GMT. "London had more shorts," commented one trader.
In New York the upward movement led by speculative buying accelerated after May broke through chart resistance at $1,440, triggering buy stops.
It was also helped by the dollar's weakness against sterling, prompting some arbitrage buying in the CSCE market.
Technically, if London can stay above 1,000 stg it will try to conquer the 1,035-37 area, which hold the key for any significant gains.
On the downside, a chart gap between 989 and 982 may run into sell-stops and send prices to 950, analysts said.
